name: language-rooting-open-points
body:
Design decisions for language rooting (do NOT re-litigate; every point below is now resolved — PINNED or DECIDED — none is deferred).

(1) The root id string — PINNED: the `lang_switch` id verbatim (`go`/`java`/`cpp`/`rust`/`ts`/`js`/`csharp`/`py`/`md`) is both the `Language` node FQN and the FQN prefix — one identity, no second alias that could drift, consistent with domain.value.language-id. The alternative (a human-readable display root such as `python`/`javascript` differing from the id) introduces a mapping and is not chosen.

(2) The `Language` node's own FQN — PINNED: the bare id (`rust`), reserved because every module FQN now begins with `<id>.` so no module can occupy it. The alternative `language.rust` is recorded but not chosen; changing it changes the observable Language FQN.

(3) The unified JS/TS frontend's root id — DECIDED (Human): one id PER STREAM — `js` for a JS-only repo, `ts` otherwise (whatever auto-detection selected). The root is the id of the `lang_switch` stream that produced the modules: a mixed JS+TS repo that auto-detection scans once under `ts` roots all its modules under `ts`, and a JS-only repo roots under `js`. There is no single always-`ts` identity and no separate per-file rooting — the root is exactly the id that stream declared. Consistent with domain.value.language-id and requirements.requirement.js-ts-language-plumbing.

(4) Markdown module root — DECIDED: a markdown Module renders as `md.` + its directory's absolute path (a dotted root followed by a `/`); there is no separate path form for markdown modules. See domain.value.module-fqn-prefix (2)/(3) and requirements.requirement.markdown-sections-as-symbols.

(5) UnresolvedTarget FQNs are NOT rooted (foreign symbol names are not project identities) — a deliberate decision. If a foreign target's name equals a bare language id (e.g. `rust`), the Language node is inserted via `insert_node`, whose existing UnresolvedTarget-replacement rule applies (a real declaration replaces the placeholder).

(6) The `implemented-by` migration is authored on this branch, but the rooted code universe only becomes real after the branch re-scan; the plan must sequence it (requirements.constraint.implemented-by-migration-sequence).

(7) The markdown File FQN and all code File FQNs stay their absolute paths (not language-rooted) — files are unique by path, so no cross-language File collision exists; only module and symbol FQNs are rooted. If a rooted File FQN is ever wanted, that is a separate decision.
